en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Great Chapter 13:
The Question on the Characteristics of Mindfulness (Sati-lakkhaṇa-pañha)
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of mindfulness?
"Its characteristic, Great King, is non-forgetfulness, and its characteristic is grasping," he replied.
“How, venerable sir, does mindfulness have the characteristic of not forgetting?

“Mindfulness, great king, when it arises, does not forget wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, and dark and bright states with their counterparts, [thinking]:
‘These are the four foundations of mindfulness; these are the four right efforts; these are the four bases for spiritual power...’”
‘These are the five faculties, these are the five powers, these are the seven factors of enlightenment, this is the noble eightfold path,
this is serenity, this is insight, this is true knowledge, this is liberation.
Then the practitioner of yoga cultivates those states that should be cultivated and does not cultivate those states that should not be cultivated.
“He cultivates those states that should be cultivated and does not cultivate those states that should not be cultivated.
It is in this way, Great King, that mindfulness has the characteristic of non-forgetfulness.
“Give me a simile,” [the King said].
“Just as, Great King, the treasurer of a wheel-turning monarch reminds the king of his glory morning and evening, saying:
‘Sire, you have so many elephants, so many horses, so many chariots, so many foot-soldiers, so much bullion, so much gold, and so much property; may the Lord remember that.’”

Just as a treasurer does not overlook his property, even so, Great King, mindfulness, when arising, does not overlook wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright, or mixed phenomena:
"These are the four foundations of mindfulness; these are the four right efforts; these are the four bases for psychic power..."
‘These are the five faculties, these are the five powers, these are the seven factors of enlightenment, this is the noble eightfold path,
this is serenity, this is insight, this is true knowledge, this is liberation. Thereupon,
the practitioner of yoga cultivates those states that should be cultivated and does not cultivate those states that should not be cultivated.
“He cultivates those things that should be cultivated and does not cultivate those things that should not be cultivated.
It is in this way, Great King, that mindfulness has the characteristic of not being distracted.
“Venerable sir, how does mindfulness have the characteristic of grasping?”
“Mindfulness, Great King, when arising, examines the courses of wholesome and unwholesome states: ‘These states are beneficial; these states are harmful.
These states are helpful; these states are unhelpful.
Thereupon, the practitioner of yoga dispels the unwholesome states and adopts the wholesome states.”
“It dispels states that are unhelpful and takes hold of states that are helpful.
It is in this way, Great King, that mindfulness has the characteristic of taking hold.
“Give me a simile,” he said.
“Just as, great king, the counselor-treasure of a wheel-turning monarch knows what is beneficial and what is harmful to the king, thinking: ‘These things are beneficial to the king;
these are harmful. These are helpful;
these are unhelpful’—thereupon he removes what is harmful and adopts what is beneficial.”
It discards what is unhelpful and embraces what is helpful.
In the same way, Great King, when mindfulness arises, it tracks the courses of beneficial and harmful states, discerning: "These states are beneficial; these states are harmful.
These states are helpful; these states are unhelpful."
Then the practitioner of yoga dispels unwholesome states and takes up wholesome states.
He dispels non-beneficial states and takes up beneficial states.
In this way, Great King, mindfulness has the characteristic of taking up.
“Great King, this was also said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, mindfulness, indeed, I declare to be all-beneficial.
“You are clever, venerable Nāgasena,” he said.
The Thirteenth Question on the Characteristics of Being.
